original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-covering-permanence}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A composition of coverings in $\text{SR}(\mathcal{C})$
is a covering.
\item If $K \to L$ is a covering in $\text{SR}(\mathcal{C})$
and $L' \to L$ is a morphism, then $L' \times_L K$ exists
and $L' \times_L K \to L'$ is a covering.
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has products of pairs, and
$A \to B$ and $K \to L$ are coverings in $\text{SR}(\mathcal{C})$,
then $A \times K \to B \times L$ is a covering.
\end{enumerate}
Let $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Then (1) and (2) holds for
$\text{SR}(\mathcal{C}, X)$ and (3) holds if $\mathcal{C}$
has fibre products.

review_note: Independent theorem-only proof-safe review of pinned hypercovering.tex L467 and Stage A logical fields: A hypercover in semi-representable families gives local epimorphisms on the sheafifications of each matching-level map after Yoneda coproduct F, including degree zero, degree one, and all n+1≥2. Stage A retains all three source clauses and F's independent definition.
statement:
For an indexed family $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ in a category $\mathcal C$, write $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C)$ for the category of semi-representable families, and let $F$ be the functor sending such a family to the presheaf $\coprod_{i\in I}h_{U_i}$ (hypercovering.tex L110–155).
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site with fibre products.
Let $X \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $K$ be a hypercovering of $X$.
Consider the simplicial object $F(K)$ of $\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$,
endowed with its augmentation to the constant simplicial presheaf $h_X$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism of presheaves $F(K)_0 \to h_X$ becomes
a surjection after sheafification.
\item The morphism
$$
(d^1_0, d^1_1) :
F(K)_1
\longrightarrow
F(K)_0 \times_{h_X} F(K)_0
$$
becomes a surjection after sheafification.
\item For every $n \geq 1$ the morphism
$$
F(K)_{n + 1} \longrightarrow (\text{cosk}_n \text{sk}_n F(K))_{n + 1}
$$
turns into a surjection after sheafification.
\end{enumerate}
A hypercovering of an object $X$ in a site $\mathcal C$ with fibre products means a simplicial object $K$ of $\mathrm{SR}(\mathcal C,X)$ whose level-zero family covers $X$ and for each $n\ge0$ whose morphism $K_{n+1}\to (\mathrm{cosk}_n\mathrm{sk}_nK)_{n+1}$ is a covering (hypercovering.tex L345–359).
